verdicts.reason: A is the original's stacked layout pushed into the left third: a wide dead gap in the middle, a small can floating at the far right, and the legal line centred under nothing, so it reads as a stretched square rather than a banner. B reads properly left to right (can, headline, CTA on the circle), but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow drops below the subhead and the legal text is shrunk to an illegible ~6px.

B buries the CTA: 'Shop Sale' shrinks to a tiny pill in the bottom-right corner, jammed against legal copy broken into five cramped lines, while the large circle sits empty. A wastes the middle of the canvas and keeps the stretched-square structure, but its hierarchy and CTA stay intact.

A shrinks the product can to a thumbnail-sized icon next to the legal text, so the key imagery is lost, and the fine print is too small to read; the eyebrow also drops below the subhead. B keeps the product and a clear hierarchy, though it leaves a big empty middle and the legal line is centred off the left column.
